member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore
member.summary: Per-user revocation stamp store. The stamp is the source of truth for "are this user's tokens still valid": it is baked into the access token at login and checked on every request. Backed by Redis for a cheap per-request read, with the database (User.SessionStamp) as the durable source of truth and a fail-safe fallback when Redis is unavailable.

member.summary: Returns the user's current stamp, creating and persisting one if the user has none yet. Used when minting a token so the token always carries a valid stamp.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore.RotateAsync(System.Int32,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Rotates the user's stamp (new value persisted to the database and written through to the cache), instantly invalidating every access token that carried the old stamp. Called on password change, role change, lock and deletion. Call it after the transaction that revokes the sessions has committed (never inside it), so a concurrent request can never re-cache the old stamp.

member.summary: Validates a stamp presented by a token against the user's current stamp (Redis, with a database fallback). Returns true when they match.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ITransactionRunner
member.summary:
Runs a unit of database work inside a real transaction that the transaction interceptor opens on the (proxied) implementation. Handlers use this to keep ONLY their DB mutations transactional while doing external work (cache writes, notifications, e-mail) AFTER the commit, instead of wrapping the whole handler in [Transaction] (which would drag those external calls inside the transaction).
Milvasoft interception is proxy-based, so the transaction only fires when the method is invoked through this injected interface. A private [Transaction] method on the handler itself would NOT open a transaction: a same-instance call bypasses the proxy (self-invocation), so the interceptor never runs.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ITransactionRunner.RunAsync(System.Func{System.Threading.Tasks.Task})

member.param: The database work to run transactionally.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Extensions.StoreasyExtensions.DataUriRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^data:(?<mediatype>[\w/+.-]+);base64,(?<data>[a-zA-Z0-9+/]+={0,2})$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match the string "data:".
○ "mediatype" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [+\--/\w] atomically at least once.
○ Match the string ";base64,".
○ "data" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [+/-9A-Za-z] atomically at least once.
○ Match '=' atomically at most 2 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Extensions.StoreasyExtensions.ReplaceAndToLowerRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
\s+
Explanation:
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Extensions.StoreasyExtensions.UrlRegex
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(ht|f)tp(s?)\:\/\/[0-9a-zA-Z]([-.\w]*[0-9a-zA-Z])*(:(0-9)*)*(\/?)([a-zA-Z0-9\-\.\?\,\'\/\\\+&%\$#_]*)?$
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "ht".
○ Match 'f'.
○ Match the string "tp".
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match 's' atomically, optionally.
○ Match the string "://".
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [\-.\w] greedily any number of times.
○ Match an ASCII letter or digit.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 4th capture group.
○ Match ':'.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ 5th capture group.
○ Match the string "0-9".
○ 6th capture group.
○ Match '/' greedily, optionally.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ 7th capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [#-'+-9?A-Z\\_a-z] atomically any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.CacheKeys
member.summary: Builds every Redis key of the application, always as {prefix}:{key} with the prefix of , so applications that share one Redis never read or overwrite each other's entries (revocation stamps, rate limit counters, the feature flag cache). The [Cache] interceptor gets the same prefix through its key configurator. A new Redis key is added here, never written as a literal at the call site.
member.remarks: A service that must reach another application's keys on purpose (an admin API that revokes the tokens of the main API's users) creates a second instance with that application's options instead of repeating the key format.

member.remarks:

Guideline\s+(?<code>\d+(?:\.\d+){0,3})(?:\s*\([a-z0-9]+\))*(?:[ \t]*[-:][ \t]*(?<title>[^\r\n]+))?
Options:
RegexOptions.IgnoreCase
Explanation:

○ Match a character in the set [Ii].
○ Match a character in the set [Dd].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [Ll].
○ Match a character in the set [Ii].
○ Match a character in the set [Nn].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.
○ "code" capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Loop greedily at most 3 times.
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Loop greedily any number of times.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ Match '('.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-Za-z\u212A] atomically at least once.
○ Match ')'.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match a character in the set [\t ] atomically any number of times.
○ Match a character in the set [\-:].
○ Match a character in the set [\t ] greedily any number of times.
○ "title" capture group.
○ Match a character in the set [^\n\r] atomically at least once.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Utils.Helpers.UserUniqueConstraintHelper
member.summary: Maps a unique-index violation on Users to the message key the pre-insert checks would have returned. The check-then-insert in CreateUser is racy by nature: two requests can pass the "is this username taken?" query at the same time and only the database can reject the second one (23505). Without this, that loser gets a generic "duplicate data" answer instead of "this username is already taken".

member.summary: Whether (or its inner exception, as EF wraps it) is a unique violation (23505) of the index . For set based updates (ExecuteUpdateAsync) that race on a unique column outside the user table, e.g. an organization slug; this class is the one place the application layer reads Npgsql.
